rect.style: stroke: none; fill: #FFFFFF;

g.text: The same fence can produce very different forms of
Module imports fell 76% (January-August 2026 vs 2024) and moved from the four countries hit by
the 2025 orders to new sources, led in 2026 by Africa, Philippines, Indonesia (estimated split);
US module capacity (not output) rose, but almost no cells are made at home. China's share of
lithium-ion imports fell from 72% to 39%, mostly to Japan and Korea; Malaysia and Thailand, where
most recent battery FDI has Chinese parents, also gained. Origin diversified more than ownership.

g.text: Country of origin is not ownership: in Malaysia, 14 of 16 battery-manufacturing FDI projects have a
Chinese parent (70% of disclosed capital); in Thailand, 9 of 12 battery-manufacturing FDI projects
have a Chinese parent (95% of disclosed capital).
B. Batteries: lithium-ion imports by origin
Panel A events: (1) Duty-free moratorium on SE Asian cells and modules ends, 06 Jun 2024; (2) Section 301: China modules to 50%, 27
Sep 2024; (3) AD/CVD orders: Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, 24 Jun 2025; (4) IEEPA tariffs end; Section 122 10%, 24 Feb 2026;
(5) Section 301 forced-labour action 10-12.5%, 24 Jul 2026; (6) AD/CVD deposits: India, Indonesia, Laos, 05 Nov 2026; (7) Section
232: 15% + minimum price $0.38/W, 04 Dec 2026 (dashed: after the latest Census month, August 2026).
Panel A: US imports for consumption of HTS 8541.43.0010 (crystalline-silicon modules) from Census; imports from countries outside the
Trade War Tracker's 30 partners (Cambodia, Laos, the Philippines, Africa) are the Census remainder split by each country's monthly
share of US imports of HS 8541.43 in UN Comtrade. Africa: mainly Ethiopia, Kenya and Nigeria. Capacity: operating nameplate module
capacity (SEIA/Wood Mackenzie, secondary source), not output; production was about 12 GW in 2024 and 31 GW in 2025 (Wood Mackenzie
via NREL); crystalline-silicon cell capacity was about 3 GW in mid-2026.
Panel B: HTS 8507.60 (cells and packs cannot be separated in trade data). Ownership: NEIS CM-FDI project database (battery
manufacturing projects, all statuses, capital weighted by project attribution); it covers projects announced since about 2017, not
Sources: US Census Bureau (via the Trade War Tracker); UN Comtrade; SEIA/Wood Mackenzie US Solar Market Insight; NREL Solar Industry
Updates; Federal Register; NEIS CM-FDI database.
